layers.note: A small native population grows on the dry prairies and oak woodland of the south Puget Sound glacial outwash.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: On the level outwash plains rather than slopes.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −9 °C, gone by −14 °C, up to about 10 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Cold-hardy: lows to about −34 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −42 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 14.5 to 25 °C; gone below 12 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,800 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,100.

degree_days_5.note: About 800 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 400: from the lowlands to the montane forest.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.3, gone by 0.2.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; across its range at most about 0.7 of the year's precipitation falls in summer, gone by 0.9.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Ponderosa pine grows through the interior West from British Columbia to Mexico, on warm, dry sites with hot summers; in western Washington only on the prairies of the south Sound (Silvics of North America, vol. 1). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
